newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA's political arm warns conflict may worsen.
newsitem.headline: ETA's political arm warns conflict may worsen.

text.p: The political arm of Basque guerrilla group ETA warned on Tuesday that government attempts to isolate the rebels after the killing of a young politician could exacerbate their long-running conflict with Spain.

"The strategy of lynching and the hunt for (ETA) militants or sympathisers, which politicians and media are encouraging, is not going to solve the problem and instead risks a dangerous aggravation of it," Herri Batasuna said in a statement.

ETA's killing of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco has sparked a national outrage, expressed in three days of massive street protests across Spain. The government has vowed to isolate the rebels and crack down on their network of supporters.
Angry Basques, long intimidated by the violent separatists, have attacked offices and sympathisers of the group since Blanco's death.

Herri Batasuna said it was not "happy" about the killing. However, it added the recent events must be seen in the context of "the Spanish government's intransigence" over a key ETA demand -- the transfer of 500 ETA prisoners scattered around Spain to Basque prisons.
"We cannot forget the intransigence of (Prime Minister Jose Maria) Aznar's Spanish government in the face of Basque demands for the repatriation of Basque political prisoners," Herri Batasuna said.
The party said the government could have avoided the fatal outcome by simply transferring the prisoners.
It added that dialogue was still the best way to resolve the 29-year conflict in which ETA has killed more than 800 people in its struggle for an independent Basque state.
"The solution is not in isolating or criminalising the radical left but negotiating," an HB spokesman said at a news conference following a party meeting in San Sebastian.

ETA guerillas abducted Blanco, a Basque town councillor, on Thursday and threatened to execute him in 48 hours unless the government met their demands on the repatriation of prisoners. The government refused and rebels shot him just after the deadline passed.
His body was found bound and dumped on a mountain roadside with two bullets in his brain. He died 12 hours later.
More than two million people took to the streets on Monday in Madrid and Barcelona in one of the largest nationwide demonstrations in Spanish history to condemn the killing.
